one_liner: Header-only C++20 bitset adding fast first_one/first_zero bit-scan that std::bitset lacks above 64 bits.
what_it_does: std::bitset has no way to find the first set or unset bit for sizes above 64 (only to_ullong() plus countr_zero works at 64 bits and below). better_bitset is a single C++20 header defining a templated BitSet<N> backed by a std::array of native unsigned integers, adding first_one()/first_zero() bit-scan methods alongside the usual all/any/none/count/size/set/reset/flip/to_string API. It is not a drop-in replacement: bitwise operators (&, |, ^, ~) and std::bitset's mutable reference-proxy type are absent.
how_it_is_fast: first_one()/first_zero() call std::countr_zero()/std::countr_one() on each 64-bit (or smaller) storage chunk instead of the .test(i) bit-by-bit loop std::bitset forces on scans above 64 bits. On x86 these compile to a single hardware bit-scan instruction (the BSF/TZCNT family) per chunk, turning an O(N) per-bit test into O(N/64) chunk-level instructions. No SIMD or manual vectorization beyond whatever the compiler emits for those built-ins.
when_to_use: Fixed-size bitsets above 64 bits where you need the position of the first set/unset bit (e.g. slot allocation) without hand-writing a scan loop
Bitsets of 16 bits or fewer, where the smaller backing integer type (uint8_t/uint16_t) saves a few bytes versus std::bitset
You're willing to vendor a single ~200-line header and require only C++20, with no upstream support expected
Reference/inspiration for implementing your own countr_zero/countr_one-based bit-scan rather than using the library directly
N is not tiny: the measured gains hold from N=8 up through N=8192 in the authors' own benchmark
when_not_to_use: You need bitwise operators (&, |, ^, ~) between bitsets — not implemented
You need std::bitset's assignable reference proxy (bs[i] = true) — operator[] here is const-only
You need a maintained dependency — inactive since last commit 2022-04-08, 8 stars, two open issues with no response
You need to ship/vendor code under a known license — no LICENSE file exists and an open issue (#4) asking for one is unanswered
Your bitsets are consistently very small (N=4) — the authors' own benchmark shows better_bitset ~1.6x slower than std::bitset there

integration.dependencies: none (Google Benchmark is only required to build the optional benchmark target)
integration.min_toolchain: C++20 (cxx_std_20 required; uses std::countr_zero/std::countr_one/std::popcount from <bit> and a requires-clause template constraint)
integration.platforms: any (portable C++20 <bit> functions; the only benchmark run was on x86-64, no architecture-specific intrinsics in the header)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — implements test/all/any/none/count/size/set/reset/flip/to_string plus first_one/first_zero, but lacks bitwise operators and std::bitset's reference-proxy type

gotchas: No LICENSE file in the repo; an open, unanswered GitHub issue (#4, filed 2024-11-03) asks the maintainer to add one — treat the code as look-but-don't-ship
Open issue #3 (2024-10-01, unaddressed) disputes the correctness of first_one/first_zero for some bit patterns; unresolved since the repo has had no commits since 2022
Benchmark numbers are self-reported with no stated compiler or optimization flags (the CMakeLists sets neither CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE nor compile options), so real gains under -O2/-O3 may differ
Only smaller than std::bitset for N<=16; at N=4 in the authors' own benchmark it was slower than std::bitset's naive loop (405ns vs 250ns)
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick better_bitset over plf::bitset only if you want a single tiny header with zero build configuration and care solely about first_one/first_zero on fixed-size bitsets above 64 bits; plf::bitset covers more operations (set_range/reset_range, shifts) with gains measured on both GCC and MSVC and is the more complete std::bitset alternative in this catalog. For runtime-sized bitsets use sul::dynamic_bitset or BitLib instead (they target std::vector<bool>), and for sparse/succinct workloads use CRoaring or pasta::bit_vector.
verified_claims_summary: First-party Google Benchmark (compiler/flags unstated) on a 20-logical-core ~3.6GHz host: better_bitset::first_one() beats a naive std::bitset .test(i) bit-by-bit loop from N=8 through N=8192 (e.g. 18,134ns vs 953,294ns at N=8192, ~52.6x; 1,789ns vs 128,450ns at N=1024, ~71.8x), but is ~1.6x slower than std::bitset at N=4 (405ns vs 250ns). The mean of the 13 per-size ratios is ~34x, well below the README's claimed '60x average'.
status_note: Abandoned since its last commit on 2022-04-08 (8 stars); no LICENSE file exists and a 2024 issue asking for one is unanswered, so it's readable reference code, not something to vendor as-is.
